title: Differential Prefetch Governor with Staged Eviction and Tiered Safety Locks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a per-tenant and per-route adaptive prefetch governor that issues automatic batching/caching recommendations and can safely apply those configs with a staged-eviction rollback mechanism and tier-based safety locks. This ticket covers the runtime governor, the recommendation engine hooks, allowlist/denylist integration, and the operational playbook for gradual rollout and automated rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime exposes a per-tenant 'prefetch_score' and 'soft-evict' flag available in route metadata. 2) Recommendation engine can emit JSON suggestions for batching window, prefix-cache TTL, and prefetch budget per route. 3) Rollout controller supports staged-eviction (percent-based gradual revert) and automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions. 4) Admins can declare tiered safety locks (enterprise/standard/free) that restrict allowed recommendation classes. 5) End-to-end integration tests and a dry-run mode exist and pass in CI.
steps: Design runtime API: add PrefetchGovernor interface with score(), recommendConfig(), applyDelta()
Implement recommendation adapter that consumes telemetry (cost/token, cache hit rate, p50/p95 latency) and outputs candidate configs
Add allowlist/denylist lookup: route and customer-level controls for enabling/disabling prefetch/batching recommendations
Implement staged-eviction rollback: apply changes in graduated steps (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with health probes between steps
Add tiered safety locks: map customer tiers to allowed recommendation families and minimum thresholds
Instrument dashboards/alerts: create Grafana panels for regression detection and a synthetic probe that exercises hot routes
Create dry-run simulation harness and run against production trace replay for 7 days before canary
Canary rollout: 5 customers -> 20 customers -> 100 customers with manual gating and automatic rollback rules
Document runbook and operator commands for emergency revert and audit
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive prefetch reduces token cost but can increase tail latency and memory pressure. Staged-eviction focuses on minimizing customer-visible regressions by reverting a small percentage of traffic first.
We prefer 'soft-evict' semantics over immediate cache purges to avoid sudden performance cliffs for KV-backed caches.
Tiered safety locks let us ship recommendations quickly for low-risk tiers while requiring manual review for 'enterprise' tier customers.
This work relies on improved telemetry granularity from ENG-84021 and the dry-run sandbox from ENG-84021 and ENG-740000.
Measurement signals used by the recommender: token_cost_per_request, prefix_cache_hit_rate, p50_response_ms, p95_response_ms, memory_pressure_pct, request_drop_rate.
Rollback triggers: >10% p95 latency regression over baseline OR >15% drop in cache-hit rate OR increase in error-rate >1% absolute within 15-minute window.
Owner escalation: on rollback, system opens ENG incident template and notifies on #ops-cost-optimization channel. Engineers must include histogram snapshots and recent PRs that touched the governor.
Edge cases: multi-tenant routes where a single noisy tenant skews route-level signals -> recommender computes tenant-delta metrics (tenant vs route baseline) and issues tenant-scoped suggestions.
Operational constraint: 'allowlist' entries can be pinned to 'never-prefetch' for compliance-sensitive customers.
Performance budget: initial staged canary must not increase 95th percentile latency by more than 5ms for guarded routes (defined per-catalog).

Related research note: a brief experiment with k=8 batching window reduced per-token cost by 12% for high-reuse routes, but increased p95 by 8ms; staged-eviction mitigated customer complaints during the test.

This ticket intentionally diverges from previous 'policy engine' designs by focusing on non-blocking, reversible prefetched state changes instead of policy-wide immediate enforcement. The goal is to be conservative by default and provide fast remediation paths.
UX: Console will show 'Suggested prefetch change' with reason, expected cost delta, and a one-click 'dry apply to canary' button for owners with proper RBAC.
Data retention: store simulated-run results for 30 days for audit and regression analysis.
Security: no secrets involved; KMS not required, but audit logs must be retained for 90 days for enterprise customers per compliance request.
